body:
Please provide an MRP to make this easier to test and fix:
- A small Godot project which reproduces the issue, with no unnecessary files included. Be sure to not include the `.godot` folder in the archive (but keep `project.godot`).
- Having an MRP is very important for contributors to be able to reproduce the bug in the same way that you are experiencing it. When testing a potential fix for the issue, contributors will use the MRP to validate that the fix is working as intended.
- Drag and drop a ZIP archive to upload it (max 10 MB). **Do not select another field until the project is done uploading.**
- **Note for C# users:** If your issue is *not* C#-specific, please upload a minimal reproduction project written in GDScript. This will make it easier for contributors to reproduce the issue locally as not everyone has a .NET setup available. 

This is far too complicated and there's far too many potential configuration details to test without an MRP

Please add MRPs in future issue reports

> Please provide an MRP to make this easier to test and fix:

I can’t provide more information because this happens randomly. I think it can probably be reproduced in any project if someone takes the time to check. After writing about a dozen issues for Godot, I tend to believe it’s just another case where something “lazy-updates,” as I’ve often been told you like to “optimize” that way.

So, if this isn’t meant to be a discussion and you, like me, see it as a real bug, then most likely the problem lies in lazy updating. However, I don’t remember this issue occurring before, so my brain tells me that something here isn’t working the way it used to.

> if someone takes the time to check

We can't spend time doing triage on something that *might* happen, we get dozens of issues every day

Without some way to replicate this we can't do anything, but there aren't any lazy updates as far as I know

I see this as a bug but we can't spend time chasing down hard to pinpoint bugs with minimal information 

But if you can confirm that this happens in a completely new project with basic setup then we can leave this open and see if someone can take the time to test it

> > if someone takes the time to check
> 
> We can't spend time doing triage on something that _might_ happen, we get dozens of issues every day
> 
> Without some way to replicate this we can't do anything, but there aren't any lazy updates as far as I know
> 
> I see this as a bug but we can't spend time chasing down hard to pinpoint bugs with minimal information
> 
> But if you can confirm that this happens in a completely new project with basic setup then we can leave this open and see if someone can take the time to test it

Well, you don’t have to do it, besides, as far as I know, it’s not only the Godot team that fixes issues. There have been many cases where ordinary users found time to fix things themselves. That also means that I, as a regular user, am simply reporting that such a bug exists so that you and others are aware of it — I’m not forcing you to fix it, and it might not even bother me personally. I’ll also open an issue anyway if something does interfere, or if I find a connection or a way to solve it, and so on.

But I also don’t understand what exactly was unclear in my explanation. I specified the exact version and why I think so, and I’ve been through about ten versions of Godot — I simply don’t recall this ever happening before. So, based on my experience with Godot and the many issues I’ve written and seen, including those written by you and your team, I believe this is a lazy update, as usual.

Simply put, before, when I saved a scene, I immediately saw updates reflected in other scenes, but in this case, it’s the second time I’ve encountered this kind of issue. This time I managed to catch that the model wasn’t updating; the first time, I think it was something in the GUI — I don’t quite remember — but I recalled it was a recurring bug and decided to document it for you. In Godot, this usually means that the update mechanism failed to trigger, as has happened dozens of times with the GUI and in many other areas. By the way, I believe I even created an issue about scenes/models/textures not being re-rendered (#109332), so I wouldn’t be sure this isn’t a similar mechanism where, for some reason, it just doesn’t update.

Making bug reports is always appreciated but they have to be actionable to not clutter the system, you don't have to add details but if you can't pin down the details then it's not going to be easy for anyone else to do it either, and since you have experienced this it'd be great if you could pin down how to replicate it, unfortunately this doesn't really help in making any progress on pinpointing what causes it

I have never written an issue report related to lazy updates so I'm not sure what you are talking about
